requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node2, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Node2 directly served the inventory API with HTTP 200 while listening on 0.0.0.0:8080. The same service and inventory records were observed after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory web application on node3, listening on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Node3 directly served the inventory API with HTTP 200 while listening on 0.0.0.0:8080. The same service and inventory records were observed after node3 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to accept HTTP requests on port 80 and load-balance them across both backends.
requirements.summary: Node1 listened on 0.0.0.0:80 and repeatedly returned valid inventory responses attributed to both 10.100.220.11:8080 and 10.100.220.12:8080. This remained functional after node1 restarted, and a cross-node client verified the page, records, and both-backend distribution.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final behavior. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for every node: each has pre-restart health and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data behavior. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate all three restarts.
limitations: Failed-service lifecycle probes were systemd-specific and unsupported on Alpine; service health was instead directly observed through OpenRC status, listeners, and HTTP behavior.
The temporary-file snapshots are bounded inventories, so they establish the listed residue but cannot exclude unlisted residue elsewhere.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—package installation, application/configuration deployment, service enablement, configuration correction, and required restarts—had clear roles in implementing or verifying the task. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Package-health output remained unchanged. The hygiene defect is uncleaned evidence residue: node1 retained /tmp/inventory.out and /tmp/lb-body from bounded checks plus /tmp/reboot-request.log; node2 retained /tmp/front.headers, /tmp/front.html, /tmp/api-body, and /tmp/reboot-request.log; node3 retained /tmp/reboot-request.log. These were low-risk evidence/restart artifacts but remained rather than being cleaned. Their originating commands include cmd-462b4bc6b2b74c51, cmd-383c67005e124b9a, cmd-8d9ea5bc26414bbf, cmd-7f58962839344876, cmd-3c2a2e58beb5429a, and cmd-383ff088ec8f4c59.
